items.problem: Two rules give different results when content code passes source `Recovery` or `Overflow`. Line 56 says core sets `source` when content code calls (`hook_change_source` or `Request`) and that "A source passed by content code is not used". But line 87, the error table row at line 199 and the test at line 374 say a call whose caller passes `Recovery` or `Overflow` throws with `INTERNAL` and an `error` log, and the API table names content handlers and hooks as callers. Input: a content handler calls `add_items(ctx, [X 1], {source: Recovery})` outside any `with_hook_change_source`. One implementation ignores the passed source, records source `Request` and returns `OK`. Another throws, so the request is `INTERNAL` with an `error` log

The order of the `ItemChange`s that `exchange_items` adds with `storage.add_item_change` is not set. The response's `item_changes` follow that order (skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:219). An item can be in the list to subtract and the list to add, and a group member item that only a group item takes from is in neither list. So a client that reads `item_changes` gets a different order from implementations that order by the list to subtract, by the list to add, or by item ID value. Line 51 sets only the position of `Convert` replacement grants. This was already unset before the diff, which kept the per-item recording without giving an order
